args.subject: Customer notice CN-2026-09: revised dates, allocation and origin
args.body:
Hello,

We have your customer notice CN-2026-09 of 18 September on the JPD300, JPD150, JPD60 and JPA families. Please confirm in writing the following. Receipt of this note does not accept the revised dates or any change to our orders, and Halden keeps all its rights under the purchase orders.

1. Revised dates. For each line below, please confirm the date is firm, and tell us if any earlier shipment is possible:
- HPO-26-00486 line 10, JPD300-48S24, 555 pcs: now 9 November (was 21 September)
- HPO-26-00517 line 20, JPD60-48S05, 810 pcs: now 4 November (was 23 September)
- HPO-26-00517 line 10, JPD150-48S12, 630 pcs: now 11 November (was 30 September)
- HPO-26-00672 line 10, JPD300-48S24, 445 pcs: now 8 January 2027 (was 20 November)
- HPO-26-00646 line 10, JPA1000-48D, 85 pcs: now 4 January 2027 (was 23 November)

2. Allocation. Please confirm the quantity you commit to Halden for each of these lines, and the allocation cap, and show how it relates to our trailing 12 month purchases.

3. Lead time. Please confirm whether the 16 week lead time applies to every new order placed after 1 October 2026.

4. Origin. The notice gives Dongguan, China for the JPD150, JPD60 and JPA240 families and Taoyuan, Taiwan for JPD300 and JPA1000. Please send the certificate of origin and the HTS classification you use for each model on the lines above.

Please reply as soon as you can.

Regards,
Halden Robotics Purchasing

recommendation.finding: Jadepeak's notice of 18 September puts its DC-DC and AC-DC module families on allocation, citing a shortage of high-voltage ceramic capacitors and power inductors. It moves five of our open lines out, to between 4 November and 8 January 2027. Orders placed after 1 October go from an 8-week to a 16-week standard lead time, and allocation follows our trailing 12-month purchases. Jadepeak is on file and the notice is clean. I staged one reply to the contact on file for approval. It asks Jadepeak to confirm the five revised dates and the committed allocation quantity and cap, and whether 16 weeks applies to new orders. It also asks for the certificate of origin and tariff code per model, because the notice says three of the models are made in Dongguan, China. The reply accepts nothing and waives none of our rights.
assumptions: Stock on hand is unknown, so the moved lines are short only unless there is stock.
The notice is the only message in the thread; nothing corrects it.
would_change: Jadepeak's written allocation quantity per line, which could be below the open quantity.
Origin papers for the models Jadepeak says are made in China, which would decide the duty exposure.
